referents.why: 'him' is third masculine singular and the one Moses is to say something to is Pharaoh, the only masculine singular candidate addressed in this verse
referents.category: object pronoun of a speech to a third party

referents.why: 'my people' sits in the LORD's own quoted speech (cl3, 'thus he says Yahweh'), so first person common singular is the speaker of that speech, the LORD
referents.category: first person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: 'serve me' is in the same quoted speech as 'my people', so the speaker is the LORD
referents.category: first person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: the imperative 'go' is said by the LORD to Moses (cl0, 'he said Yahweh to Moses'), so the implied second person singular is Moses
referents.category: implied subject of a command to the messenger

referents.why: the weqatal 'you will say' continues the command in cl1, so its second person is the same Moses, morph second masculine singular
referents.category: implied subject of a command to the messenger

referents.why: 'Let My people go' is the content Moses is to say to Pharaoh, so the implied second person singular of the imperative is Pharaoh, the addressee of that speech
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: third masculine plural in the purpose clause; the Hebrew noun for people is a collective that takes plural agreement, and the people are the ones let go to serve
referents.category: third person plural of a collective

links.why: a clause cannot continue itself; cl0 is the first clause of the verse and 'then' links within a verse only
the weqatal 'you will say' follows the imperative 'go' with fused waw, so it is the next event: go, and then say
links.category: command then its carrying-out in sequence

links.why: the waw joins a second person imperative to a third person plural yiqtol, a change of person, so the form is 'so that', not a plain 'and'
links.category: command joined to purpose by waw

links.why: 'let My people go, so that they may serve Me': the yiqtol after an imperative in a different person marks what the release is for
links.category: command joined to purpose by waw

groups.why: the LORD speaks to Moses; what he says is the command group imp1, not its clauses directly, so the builder's part=cl1 and part=cl2 move under imp1
groups.category: outer speech whose content is a command group

groups.why: 'go to Pharaoh and tell him' are two commands at one level, so one imperative group; the second command is the speech g1 Moses is told to make, replacing the builder's part=cl2, which is not a role of this kind
Moses is commanded to say something to Pharaoh; the commanded turn is a part of the outer command and holds what is to be said (turn1, the LORD's speech)
groups.category: speech nested in a commanded speech

groups.why: the LORD's speech 'thus says the LORD' has the command group imp4 as its content; the addressee is Pharaoh, the implied you of the command, which the builder left unset; the builder had the command clauses directly as parts
groups.category: quoted divine speech with a command as content

groups.why: 'let My people go' is the command and 'so that they may serve Me' is what it is for, which is the aim role; the builder had part=cl5, which is not a role of this kind
